code:
pwd               # print the folder you are in
ls                # list what is here (ls -la also shows hidden files; in PowerShell, plain ls)
cd ~              # go to your home folder
mkdir -p ~/cs357  # make a folder for this course (in PowerShell: mkdir ~/cs357)
cd ~/cs357        # go into it
cd ..             # go up one level
description: Six commands for finding where you are, moving between folders, and making a project folder, on every system this course supports.

steps.description: These six commands cover the terminal work in every setup step. The terminal always has a current folder, and every relative path is measured from it. They work the same in every shell above, including PowerShell.
`pwd` prints the folder you are in, and `ls` lists what is here. `ls -la` also shows hidden files; in PowerShell use plain `ls`.
`cd ~` goes to your home folder. `mkdir -p ~/cs357` makes a folder for this course; in PowerShell it is `mkdir ~/cs357`.
`cd ~/cs357` goes into that folder, and `cd ..` goes up one level.
